title: Reading AhuraMazdā the way it was meant to be written

body:
# Reading AhuraMazdā the way it was meant to be written
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **AhuraMazdā** is what the evidence put back.

The mythology of AhuraMazdā is not a cycle of adventures but a grand cosmology: the creation of the world, the fall of the first man Yima, the choice offered to Zarathustra, and the final renovation (Frashokereti) when evil will be destroyed and the world made perfect. Every human moral choice participates in this cosmic drama. In the Gāthās, AhuraMazdā approaches Zarathustra and asks him to choose between the two primordial spirits: Spenta Mainyu, the holy creative spirit, and Angra Mainyu, the destructive spirit of the lie.  Zarathustra chooses good thought, good words, and good deeds, becoming the prophet of the one wise lord.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** AhuraMazdā
- **ASCII form:** ahuramazda
- **Meaning:** "Wise lord"
- **Domain of influence:** Supreme Creator, Wisdom, Light
- **Pantheon:** Zoroastrian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐬀𐬵𐬎𐬭𐬀 𐬨𐬀𐬰𐬛𐬁
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 8 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **AhuraMazdā** to *ahuramazda* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Macron: long a: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

These are the small, provable things a restoration is made of: not taste, not branding — attestation.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **AhuraMazdā** lives at [/sites/ahuramazda/](/sites/ahuramazda/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ahuramazda/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ahuramazda/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ahuramazda/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **AhuraMazdā** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Education, Research & Knowledge** — The Wise Lord of living Zoroastrian devotion; the supreme creator of a world faith.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The Wise Lord at the center of living Zoroastrian devotion.
- **Solar & Renewable Energy** — Wisdom and Light are his canonical domain; the sun and the sacred radiance are the visible signs of the Wise Lord.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Zoroastrian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Avesta — Yasna & Yashts](/texts/avesta/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/ahuramazda/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Aganjú** ([read it here](/sites/aganju/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Aígyptos** ([read it here](/sites/aigyptos/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
